titulo: Anatomy: tools, resources, and prompts; client, server, and transport
lead: Before you write code, separate the pieces. The MCP server offers three things (tools, resources, and prompts), the client lives inside the app with the model, and the transport is just the pipe. In this lesson you connect a client to the kit's server and see each piece listed.
objetivo: tell a tool, a resource, and a prompt apart, and say who is the host, client, server, and transport in your service.

aprende.t: Host, client, transport, and server: who calls whom
A tool is an action the model chooses; a resource is data the client reads; a prompt is a template the person chooses
The current protocol revision is 2026-07-28, and what changed in it
List the kit server's pieces in one command

hero_alt: Top-down view of a dark desk with a tool, a folder, and a card connected by cables to a small hub.

secoes.titulo: From the app to your service

nos.detalhe: The app where the model works: Claude Code, Codex, VS Code with an agent. It shows the tool to the model and asks for your approval before calling it.
The part of the host that speaks MCP. One client per connected server. It lists what the server offers and makes the calls.

Where the JSON-RPC messages travel. stdio: the host starts your server as a process and talks over stdin/stdout. Streamable HTTP: the server sits at a URL and handles requests. SSE as a standalone transport is something from old tutorials.
The program you write. It doesn't call any model: it just announces what it can do and answers calls.

secoes.legenda: Split of control according to the official v2 SDK documentation (Tools, Resources, and Prompts pages), read on 10/19/2026.

secoes.titulo: The three things a server offers
secoes.sub: In the kit, a fictional course class service.

texto: A function the model decides to call based on its name, description, and input schema. It can only read, or it can change something in the world.

exemplo.rot: Question that leads the model to call it
exemplo.texto: Is there an MCP class with an open seat?

texto: Read-only data, identified by a URI, that the client lists and attaches as context. The app decides what to read, not the model.
In the kit: turmas://catalogo, the whole catalog in JSON.
A ready-made request, with arguments, that the client shows for the person to choose (like a slash command or menu item).
In the kit: convite_turma, which builds the request for an invitation to a class.
If it changes something or depends on the user's question, it's a tool. If it's stable context the app can attach, it's a resource. If it's a shortcut the person triggers, it's a prompt.
Most services start with just tools, and that's fine.

secoes.titulo: Revision 2026-07-28: what changed on one screen
paragrafos: The current protocol version is 2026-07-28 (MCP versioning page, read on 10/19/2026). The previous one was 2025-11-25.

What changes the most for anyone coming from 2025: there is no more initialize handshake or session (Mcp-Session-Id); each request carries the version and capabilities in _meta; the client discovers the server with server/discover; and a server that needs to ask the user something returns input_required instead of opening its own request. Roots, Sampling, and Logging were deprecated.

The official SDK that implements this is the v2 line (@modelcontextprotocol/server and @modelcontextprotocol/client, 2.3.1, from 10/05/2026). The old @modelcontextprotocol/sdk package (1.32.1) still speaks 2025-11-25: it's what you'll find in most tutorials.

secoes.titulo: List the pieces of the kit's server
secoes.sub: You need the kit installed (lesson 2, first block). The client talks to the server in the same process, with no port.

era: modern means the client and server agreed on revision 2026-07-28. With mode: 'legacy' (the v2 client's default) they would fall back to the 2025 initialize.

exercicios.titulo: E2 · Your service in three columns
exercicios.texto: In a file named mapa-mcp.md, list what your service would expose as a tool, as a resource, and as a prompt. Mark each tool as read or consequence.

perguntas.p: Who decides to call an MCP tool?
opcoes: The server, whenever it receives new data from an external system
The model, based on the name, the description, and the schema
The person, by picking from a menu in the client
The transport, depending on the type of message that passes through the pipe
perguntas.explica: A tool is the model's choice. A menu for the person is a prompt; data the app attaches is a resource.

perguntas.p: The full class catalog, in JSON, that the app can attach as context, is what?
perguntas.explica: Stable data identified by a URI (turmas://catalogo) is a resource. If it depended on the user's question, it would be a tool.

perguntas.p: What did the 2026-07-28 revision remove from the protocol?
opcoes: The initialize handshake and the session
The tools with an input schema in JSON Schema
The JSON-RPC format of the messages between the two sides
perguntas.explica: stdio and Streamable HTTP stay; so does JSON-RPC. Gone are initialize, the session, and Mcp-Session-Id; server/discover came in.

perguntas.p: You install @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.32.1 by following a tutorial. Which revision does it speak?
opcoes: Any of them, depending on the client
perguntas.explica: The v1 line has LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION = '2025-11-25'. 2026-07-28 is in the v2 line (@modelcontextprotocol/server 2.3.1).

itens.texto: A host with a model, a client inside it, a transport, and your server.
Tool (the model chooses), resource (the client reads), prompt (the person chooses).
2026-07-28, with no initialize and no session; SDK v2 2.3.1 implements it.
